paragraphs: ) is the undisputed icon of the Ice Age tundra, a gargantuan herbivore whose thick, shaggy coat and dense layer of subcutaneous fat allow it to thrive in the harshest sub-zero climates. Standing up to four meters tall at the shoulder, this magnificent creature uses its sweeping, curved tusks to clear deep snowdrifts in search of buried grasses, mosses, and shrubbery. While generally docile when left unprovoked, a threatened herd will quickly form a defensive wall around their young, turning their immense weight and crushing tusks into a formidable wall of living muscle.
